name: Nïrwe
description:
Oppression. Rebellion. The complicated aftermath.

When the Chthonic Subcommittee came into power, their first act was to throw up walls around their Citadel spanning the Great Chasm: the miles-long scar in the earth that gave the city its name. From this stronghold their cruel edicts were issued unopposed, and through their bureaucrats and mechanical Enforcers they regulated and oppressed the use of magic throughout the land. A sad, desperate, dirty, chaotic city grew outside the walls, and with it a rising discontent.

Then came the Rising of the Bards. Through song, they spurred the people to throw down the gates and storm the Citadel. The rebels found it hastily abandoned, the Subcommittee itself having fled deep into the Chasm. Then all chambers were thrown open, and many dear friends and enchanted things long-missed were found.

So began a merry and prosperous time: an age of free magic, of discovery and joy. Without the Subcommittee to choke the curiosity of the people, magic flowed from every fingertip in every corner of the land and for every purpose, great and humble.

But the unity of the rebels was brief. Factions quickly formed and each district of the city fell under the control of gang leaders who meted out their own justice. Today, the city is a tumult of alliances, power grabs, betrayals and assassination plots.

Though the abandoned Citadel appears empty and lifeless by day, by night it seems more and more to reawaken: strange lights are seen within the walls, shapes of wandering darkness roam the edges of the Chasm and the rusting bodies of the Enforcers are seen in one place one day and found elsewhere the next. Are all these things moved by some lingering magic of the Subcommittee, by some new evil taking root there, or by some ancient power creeping back in?

hooks.name: The Weaver Sisters
hooks.description: The Weaver Sisters' Gang was one of the fiercest, most powerful organizations in Nïrwe until the eldest and fiercest of the sisters, Moonbird, didn't return from an expedition into the Chasm. Almost overnight, rival gangs moved to take over the Sisters' territory and snuff out their underlings. The two remaining sisters are organizing a clandestine search party for Moonbird, and they are paying top dollar.
hooks.gmNotes:
The first challenge will be getting from the sisters' hideout to the Chasm's mouth, which will lead Our Heroes through the territory of multiple rival gangs and through the abandoned Citadel, whose gates and grounds may or may not be guarded by mysterious threats.

The Chasm mouth should be frightening and there should be evident threats just inside, but at this point the aforementioned rival gangs should appear in pursuit, forcing Our Heroes to flee into the Chasm.

The Chasm itself can be as winding and full of peril as you choose, but ultimately, the idea is to have Our Heroes and the rival gang pursuers converge on a deep chamber simultaneously, where it's revealed that Moonbird is alive and well, and her disappearance was a ruse to lure her sisters and rivals. She seems to be possessed of (by?) some evil power. She was always the fiercest of the Sisters, but now she is turning her fury against everyone indiscriminately - even her own sisters.

It's up to you what dark power has possessed Moonbird, or whether she has gone mad with rage of her own volition. It's also up to you whether the other Weaver Sisters have the guts to subdue her and reclaim their territory back in the city.

Bonus points for making the rival gangs sympathetic - even bumbling - characters early on, setting things up for an uneasy alliance later on.

hooks.name: The Lost Songs
hooks.description:
Each year on the anniversary of the storming of the Citadel, the bards of Nïrwe converge on the site of the broken gates to participate in a competitive performance. Nearly the entire city turns out, and the winners can expect royal treatment for a whole year.

It has long been rumored that one of the high-ranking Cthonic Subcommittee members was secretly a connoisseur of the very music they worked to suppress, and had a hoard of some of the greatest songs ever composed. This hoard was never found, and some suspect the scrolls yet remain in some hidden chamber in the abandoned Citadel.

Last year's competition winner is under enormous pressure to perform well once again, and word has it that they're looking for bodyguards to accompany them on a secret songwriting expedition into the old Citadel.
hooks.gmNotes:
The bard who has hired Our Heroes should have a map that they got from a mysterious figure who spoke with an accent strongly associated with the Subcommittee. The map should lead to one of the high towers of the Citadel.

This can be a fairly straightforward adventure through the creepy abandoned Citadel, but perhaps it is not as abandoned as it seems. At the very least Our Heroes should encounter some beasts that have taken up residence there.

Throughout the Citadel, the rusting remains of the Subcommittee's mechanical Enforcers should be littered here and there, but when Our Heroes reach the upper chamber and attempt to enter, they should find it guarded by a massive, fearsome, still-functional Enforcer that is activated by their attempted entry.

Assuming they best this formidable foe, the chamber it was guarding should indeed be the resting place of the rumored scrolls. You have two options here: 1) the scrolls are amazing songs and our bard friend is sure to win the competition by using them; or 2) the scrolls contain songs that are quite bad - evidently the Subcommittee member who collected them had bad taste - and now Our Heroes must help their bard friend come up with something in time for the competition tomorrow.

If you want to widen the scope of the adventure, consider having Our Heroes discover a secret reconvening of the surviving Subcommittee members (perhaps engaged in interrogating the mysterious figure who sold the bard the scrolls?). There could be an imminent plot to unleash some deadly threat upon the gathered masses at the competition tomorrow, and a huge battle amid the performance could be the finale of the adventure.

hooks.name: The Lungfish Run
hooks.description:
Each spring, the lungfish return to the mud flats of Nïrwe's bleak harbor to spawn. They once arrived in such great numbers that you could just reach down and gather them into a sack, but the Subcommittee's over-harvesting drove them nearly to extinction.

Now there is fierce competition among gatherers on the appointed day. But even if you manage to gather a good haul, there remains the problem of getting your catch to market without being forced to hand it over to each of the gangs whose turf lies between the docks and the market.

The prices for lungfish are higher than ever this year, and word on the street is that the harvesters are looking for muscle to help them get through the net of gangs.
hooks.gmNotes:
This is all a setup for essentially a fun take on the film The Warriors. Our Heroes need to get all the way across town with their precious, fishy cargo, and must fight their way through as many diverse and assorted gangs as you care to throw at them.

Some possible gang names: The Cinder Mantises, The Brass Oxen, The Funeral Crows, The Blindfold Brotherhood, The Paper Phoenixes, The Laughing Monkeys, The River Teeth, The Moon Hare Clan.

Have fun!
